name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with a PVI of R+27
Incumbent Adrian Smith running again with a large financial edge
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 96% to win
Democratic challenger Becky Stille has minimal fundraising and no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Smith: a heavily Republican western Nebraska seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger who has raised only about $55,000. Markets agree, pricing Smith near 96%, so the race sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any unexpected incumbent retirement, scandal, or major outside spending against Smith would be the main way this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adrian Smith is seeking another term in Nebraska's heavily Republican 3rd District, which carries a partisan lean of about 27 points toward the GOP. He has raised roughly $1.8 million and holds over $1 million on hand, with modest outside support and no outside opposition spending in the race.

His challengers have raised little by comparison: Democrat Becky Stille has about $15,000 on hand, and independent and third-party candidates remain marginal. No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes an upset highly unlikely.
